EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A northerly swell produced life-threatening rip currents along the northern beaches of Puerto Rico from late December into early 2026.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 53-year-old man drowned at Ocean Park Beach after being pulled by a rip current while attempting to assist a family member in the water.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Fresh to locally strong east to northeast winds and a long-period northwesterly swell, resulted in a high risk of rip currents along northern beaches of Puerto Rico, and Culebra. Two 21 year old males were swept away by currents in Caracoles Beach, Arecibo. One was rescued with injuries and the other was found deceased.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two 21-year-old males from Corozal were swept away by rip currents at Caracoles Beach along Highway PR-681 in Arecibo. One individual was rescued by the US Coast Guard and transported to a hospital. The body of the second individual was recovered the following day, Jan 19th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Emergency Managers reported two fallen trees on Feb 28th due to breezy to windy conditions.  A building Azores High over the central Atlantic dominated the local weather pattern, and promoted these breezy to windy ESE to SE flow.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency managers reported a large fallen tree onto a house in San Isidro, Canovanas. No significant structural damage to the house was reported at the time of the incident. The incident was due to strong winds. Surface observations near the area showed wind gusts between 20 and 28 mph.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A long-period northerly swell impacted the Atlantic waters and northern coastal areas of Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands from February 18 through February 20, 2026. The swell propagated across the regional waters, producing increasing wave heights and hazardous marine conditions.||Breaking waves initially ranged from 6 to 8 feet and increased to between 10 and 12 feet as the event intensified. These conditions generated high surf and life-threatening rip currents along north- to northeast-facing beaches, including Puerto Rico, Culebra, and the northern U.S. Virgin Islands.||The most hazardous conditions occurred from February 19 to 20, when the combination of long-period swell and elevated wave energy led to dangerous coastal conditions. Impacts gradually diminished after February 20 as the swell subsided.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A rip current incident occurred at Puerto Nuevo Beach in Vega Baja during the morning of February 19, 2026. Four individuals entered the water and were swept toward deeper waters by a strong rip current. Three individuals returned safely to shore, while one was carried offshore. Search efforts continued for more than a week; however, the individual was not recovered and was classified as missing and presumed dead. This fatality was attributed to hazardous marine conditions associated with a long-period northerly swell.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broad surface high pressure over the Central Atlantic resulted in breezy conditions on January 21st with gusts up to 35 mph reported over coastal areas.  Brief, strong winds not associated with a thunderstorm were reported to affect Santa Elena neighborhood in Guayanilla that afternoon. Residential solar panels sustained damage, and several trash cans were displaced. A resident reported loud wind noise at the time of the event.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: At approximately 5:45 PM AST, a well-defined funnel cloud was observed and captured on video by the public in Barrio Piletas, Lares. Video confirmed clear rotation; however, the circulation remained aloft and did not make contact with the surface. No damage or injuries were associated with this convective feature.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A frontal boundary interacting with southerly flow produced a period of heavy rainfall across Puerto Rico from February 2 through February 4, 2026. Abundant moisture and an advective pattern supported widespread showers and periods of moderate to heavy rainfall across the region.||Significant rainfall amounts fell across portions of PR. These conditions resulted in urban and small-stream flooding, localized flash flooding, and minor landslides, particularly across the interior, southern, and western parts of Puerto Rico. Elevated streamflows were observed, with some rivers reaching action stage.

Emergency managers reported that rainfall between 1 and 3 inches triggered slope failure, resulting in debris covering the roadway and downed trees in the area. The landslide disrupted traffic on the roadway and required clearing operations.
